title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 232 (Merger and amalgamation of companies)

content.overview: Section 232 applies where a compromise or arrangement proposed under section 230 involves a merger or amalgamation of two or more companies. It requires circulation of the draft scheme, a valuation report, and consideration of reports of the Registrar, official liquidator and other regulators as applicable. The Tribunal may sanction the scheme; the order may provide for transfer of property and liabilities, allotment of shares, and dissolution of the transferor company without winding up. Fast-track mergers of eligible companies use section 233; cross-border mergers with notified jurisdictions use section 234.
content.glance: Merger/amalgamation scheme under s. 230 process + s. 232 extras: circulate scheme, valuation report, RD/OL/regulator reports; Tribunal sanction; transfer of property/liabilities; dissolution without winding up; distinct from fast-track s. 233 and cross-border s. 234.
content.study: Where an application under section 230 involves a proposed merger or amalgamation of two or more companies, the Tribunal may order meetings and, on sanction, provide for transfer of the whole or part of the undertaking, property or liabilities, allotment or appropriation of shares, continuation of legal proceedings, and dissolution of the transferor company without winding up. The company must circulate the scheme and a report of the expert as to valuation, and the Tribunal considers reports of the Registrar and official liquidator. Current-law framing: confirm the scheme is a merger/amalgamation; apply s. 230 process plus s. 232 circulation, valuation and regulatory reports; obtain Tribunal sanction; effect transfer and optional dissolution without winding up. Distinguish fast-track (s. 233) and cross-border (s. 234).

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Compromise or arrangement under s. 230 that involves merger or amalgamation of two or more companies.

sections.heading: Additional Requirements
sections.body: Circulation of draft scheme; expert valuation report; reports of Registrar, official liquidator and other regulators as applicable.

sections.heading: Sanction and Effect
sections.body: Tribunal may sanction; order may transfer property and liabilities, provide for share allotment, continue proceedings, and dissolve transferor without winding up.

sections.heading: Related Routes
sections.body: Fast-track eligible mergers: s. 233; cross-border with notified jurisdictions: s. 234.

examples.title: Amalgamation with dissolution
examples.body: Company A merges into Company B under a s. 232 scheme. The Tribunal order transfers A’s property and liabilities to B and dissolves A without winding up.

examples.title: Valuation report
examples.body: A merger scheme is circulated without an expert valuation report. Section 232 requires circulation of the scheme together with the valuation report; omission can defeat sanction.

hypotheticals.question: Must every merger go through the full Tribunal process under s. 232?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Eligible companies (e.g. small companies, holding and wholly owned subsidiary, and other notified classes) may use the fast-track route under s. 233, confirmed by the Central Government through the Regional Director, subject to the thresholds and objection process in that section.

distinctions.title: Tribunal merger (s. 232) vs fast-track merger (s. 233)
distinctions.left: Full Tribunal process with valuation and RD/OL reports
distinctions.right: Eligible classes; RD confirmation; 90% members / 9/10 creditors; objection can remit to Tribunal

misconceptions.trap: Section 232 replaces section 230 for all schemes.
misconceptions.correction: Section 232 applies where the s. 230 compromise or arrangement involves a merger or amalgamation. The meeting and majority framework of s. 230 remains the foundation; s. 232 adds merger-specific requirements and effects.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 232 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm merger/amalgamation under s. 230 process. II. Check circulation, valuation, RD/OL reports. III. Tribunal sanction and transfer/dissolution effects. IV. Distinguish s. 233/234. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Scheme; valuation; regulatory reports; sanction sought; precise relief.

examTips: Fast-track is s. 233; cross-border is s. 234.

enhancement.definition: Section 232 governs schemes under s. 230 that involve merger or amalgamation, requiring circulation of the scheme and valuation report, consideration of regulatory reports, and enabling transfer of property and dissolution without winding up on Tribunal sanction.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Mergers and amalgamations proceed through the compromise framework with added transparency, valuation and regulatory scrutiny, and can effect transfer and dissolution without a separate winding-up.
essentialIngredients: Scheme is a merger or amalgamation under s. 230 process
Circulation of scheme and valuation report
Reports of Registrar, official liquidator and regulators
Tribunal sanction; transfer and optional dissolution without winding up
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 232 is the ordinary Tribunal route for mergers and amalgamations.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm merger; apply extras; seek sanction; note alternative routes.
